fields.claim_quote: A consequence of the first characterization is that $G$ is chordal if and only if $G$ can obtained from two chordal graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, with $V(G_1) \subsetneq V(G)$ and $V(G_2) \subsetneq V(G)$, via clique pasting.
fields.explanation: The original K3 witness is preserved. The Lean graph is the complete SimpleGraph (Fin 3). Every Mathlib Walk.IsCycle has length at most three, using IsTrail.length_le_card_edgeFinset; hence there cannot be an induced cycle of length at least four. Mathlib has no separate chordal predicate in this checkout. For arbitrary actual G.Subgraph objects with proper vertex sets, their lattice union cannot be top: vertices omitted on opposite sides yield a missing cross-edge. Thus clique pasting cannot produce K3, even before imposing the additional chordality and clique-intersection constraints. The literal source does not exclude complete graphs.
fields.flaw: Every chordal graph can be obtained via clique pasting from two chordal graphs whose vertex sets are both proper subsets of its vertex set.
fields.problem: Title: Hamiltonian chordal graphs are not cycle extendible
fields.witness: Let G=K3 on {a,b,c}. It is chordal because it has no cycle of length at least 4. Suppose G is the clique pasting (union) of G1,G2 with proper vertex subsets V1,V2. Since V1∪V2={a,b,c}, choose x∉V1 and y∉V2; then x≠y. Neither G1 nor G2 can contain edge xy, contradicting xy∈E(K3).
